title: Emotion categories are contested. They are not the state.
summary: Ekman argues for basic emotions. Barrett argues emotions are constructed. Cowen and colleagues report many categories on continuous gradients, and they report that categories beat valence and arousal for recognition. HORBM's state stays the three floats.
body:
The literature this pack opened does not agree on whether emotion is a short list of kinds.

Ekman (1992) is titled "An argument for basic emotions". The PDF was not opened, so his list is not copied onto this card. The title is the view: there are basic emotions to argue for.

Barrett's abstract, opened, says the science of emotion has been using folk categories to look for a brain basis, and offers a theory of constructed emotion instead. That is her abstract's claim. The article's model is not reproduced here.

Cowen and Keltner (2017) are titled as saying self-report captures 27 categories bridged by continuous gradients. Cowen, Elfenbein, Laukka, and Keltner (2019), abstract opened, report at least 24 kinds of emotion in brief vocal bursts. They say categories, more than appraisals such as valence and arousal, organize recognition, and that the categories are bridged by smooth gradients rather than discrete cuts. A separate 2019 paper is titled as the primacy of categories in recognizing 12 emotions in speech prosody across two cultures. That body was not opened.

So a pure "categories are a mistake" reading is not what Cowen and colleagues wrote, and a pure "basic emotions are settled" reading is not what Barrett's abstract wrote. Both the many-category view and the constructed view are live.

The house state does not pick a winner. The runtime point is arousal, valence, and dominance, updated every 80 ms. A Cowen name may be an optional pin when a voice layer asks for a name. The pin is not written into memory as "this person is an anxious person", and the persona files forbid naming the caller's emotion back to them. Whether a pin may be spoken at all is open question 8 in the internal note.

The 3-bit labels already on the feeling wire (neutral, calm, joy, and the rest) are a derived view for that wire. The empathy note says the label field is full, so empathy is not a new label. They are not a second theory of emotion.

contested_views.label: Basic emotions
contested_views.summary: Ekman 1992 is an argument for basic emotions. The article was not opened, so this card does not list his categories or his criteria.

contested_views.label: Constructed emotion
contested_views.summary: Barrett's abstract argues against searching for a brain basis of folk emotion categories and names a theory of constructed emotion.

contested_views.label: Many categories on gradients
contested_views.summary: Cowen and colleagues report 27 self-report categories, at least 24 kinds in vocal bursts, and a 12-emotion prosody study. Categories organized vocal-burst recognition more than valence and arousal, and the categories were bridged by continuous gradients.

contested_views.label: House state
contested_views.summary: HORBM keeps a continuous arousal, valence, and dominance point, stepped every 80 ms. Category names are not the stored state. This is a design choice, not a finding that the other views are false.
